subject: Meteorology
title: The Tri-State Tornado
description: A quick win: understand The Tri-State Tornado.

hook.text: The 1925 Tri-State Tornado killed 695 people across Missouri, Illinois, and Indiana—the deadliest US tornado outbreak.

buildup.text: The tornado traveled 352 km in 3.5 hours—an unprecedented track length that destroyed entire towns.

discovery.text: There was no tornado warning system in 1925—the Weather Bureau didn't even use the word 'tornado' in forecasts.

twist.text: The Bureau had banned the word 'tornado' from forecasts for decades—fearing public panic would cause more harm.

climax.text: This disaster, among others, eventually forced the creation of severe weather warning systems in the late 1940s.

punchline.text: A banned word and no warnings—695 lives was the cost.

quiz.question: Why didn't the US Weather Bureau warn of tornadoes before the 1940s?
options: The word 'tornado' was banned from forecasts to avoid panic
